title: DictateIt
oneLiner: Text-to-speech dictation for people who write while listening.
claim: Reads every chunk twice - once naturally, once slowly and explicitly - and leaves a silent gap sized to what you have to write.

metrics: Prose chunked into 3 to 8 word groups at natural pause points, math into 6 token or fewer groups split on the AST
LaTeX, plain text and Unicode all reach the same AST, including fractions, roots, matrices and multi-line derivations
Write gaps scale with words or tokens, plus extra time for structures you have to draw
Three voice backends behind one interface: pyttsx3 offline, Piper offline neural, edge-tts online neural
Reads .docx equation objects directly, converting OMML to LaTeX into the same AST
proof.architecture: An input is normalised to one AST, the AST is chunked, and each chunk becomes a speech plan: a natural pass, an explicit pass that names every structure, then a measured silence. A tkinter control window shows the rendered formula, switches profiles and toggles the source text.
